item.title: Grenada, Beyond the Shore: The Living Traditions Behind the Island
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Six Senses La Sagesse, discovering Grenada means looking beyond its beaches to the people, landscapes, and traditions that give the island its character. A collection of locally rooted experiences invites guests into a more personal encounter with Grenadian life, beginning with Harvest Homestead, a visit to a two-acre organic farm led by Theresa Marryshow, head of Grenada’s local women’s farming organization. Guests learn about sustainable agriculture and the island’s food traditions while gaining insight into the work of local women farmers. The Hidden Haven excursion pairs a journey to the Seven Sisters Waterfalls with wellness and culinary elements, while the Reggae Fields Journey introduces guests to Grenadian cocoa farmers and beekeepers before inviting them to make their own cocoa balls. Together, these experiences reveal an island whose richness is found not only in its natural beauty, but in the knowledge, livelihoods, and cultural practices sustained by its communities.

The Curated Take

There is a particular depth to travel that makes room for the people who know a place best. On Grenada, a farm visit, a conversation with a beekeeper, or the making of a traditional cocoa treat can offer a more lasting connection than simply passing through a beautiful landscape. These encounters give the island’s natural appeal a human dimension, revealing the quiet richness of traditions carried forward through everyday life.

item.title: A Winter Worth Lingering For: Alpine Indulgence at Bachelor Gulch
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At The Ritz-Carlton, Bachelor Gulch, winter in Colorado’s Beaver Creek mountains extends well beyond the ski slopes. The 2026/27 season brings together alpine adventure, culinary discovery, restorative wellness, and festive traditions in a setting designed for both exhilaration and lingering fireside moments. Ski-in, ski-out access to Beaver Creek Mountain provides a natural starting point, while new experiences invite guests to explore another side of mountain life: a hands-on Cocktail Atelier with the resort’s lead mixologists, a guided Dom Pérignon and caviar tasting, and a private raclette dinner at historic Anderson Cabin. The resort’s 21,000-square-foot spa offers another kind of winter retreat, with therapeutic treatments, sound healing, red-light LED therapy, and restorative facilities. Beyond the slopes, guided snowshoe excursions and hands-on Art in Nature workshops offer opportunities to engage with the landscape at a gentler pace. Seasonal celebrations add to the atmosphere, from the annual tree lighting and holiday programming to Hanukkah observances and New Year’s Eve dining.

The Curated Take

The appeal of a mountain escape is not always measured in vertical feet or hours spent on the slopes. At Bachelor Gulch, the winter experience is shaped by the contrast between outdoor adventure and the pleasures of staying in: a private alpine dinner, a carefully guided tasting, or an evening gathered around a three-story stone fireplace. That balance gives the destination a broader appeal, making it as inviting for travelers drawn to the rituals of winter as for those who come specifically to ski.

item.title: Mui Ne Takes to the Wind: A Coastal Adventure at The Anam
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
From November through March, the Northeast Monsoon transforms Mui Ne, Vietnam, into a spectacular setting for kitesurfing, with colorful sails filling the skies above its coastline. The Anam Mui Ne is introducing a seasonal experience that brings guests closer to this distinctive coastal culture through its Windswept Adrenaline Tour. The half-day excursion begins with a private Jeep safari along the shore, continuing to Hon Rom Beach for views of the kitesurfers before a private introductory workshop at Ca Ty Beach, where certified instructors demonstrate the fundamentals of kite control on land. An expert freestyle performance follows, offering a closer look at the sport’s skill and spectacle. The afternoon concludes with a private sunset picnic by the sea. Designed for beginners as well as curious observers, the experience offers a fresh way to discover the winds, scenery, and outdoor culture that have made Mui Ne one of Asia’s leading kitesurfing destinations.

The Curated Take

Some destinations are defined by a particular relationship with the elements. In Mui Ne, the seasonal winds are more than a feature of the weather; they have shaped the coastline’s identity and drawn an international community of kitesurfers. The Anam’s experience offers an accessible introduction to that local character, balancing the energy of the sport with the quieter pleasure of watching the sails move across the water as daylight fades. It is a reminder that a memorable resort experience can begin by looking beyond the property and discovering what makes its surroundings distinctive.

item.title: “Stars Align”: Los Angeles Unveils the Slogan for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
As Los Angeles prepares to welcome the world for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games, LA28 has unveiled “Stars Align” as the official slogan for the event, capturing the meeting of athletic achievement, collective ambition, and the creative energy of its host city. Introduced through a global campaign film set to the Red Hot Chili Peppers’ “Can’t Stop,” the slogan draws on the idea that extraordinary moments emerge when years of dedication meet a defining opportunity. The film brings together iconic Los Angeles landmarks, including the Hollywood Sign and Griffith Observatory, with the city’s golden-hour light, diverse communities, and memorable moments from the history of the Games. The Olympic Opening Ceremony is scheduled for July 14, 2028, followed by the Paralympic Opening Ceremony on August 15. Los Angeles will become the third city to host the Summer Olympics three times and will welcome its first-ever Paralympic Games.

The Curated Take

A host city does more than provide venues for the Olympic Games. It becomes part of the story, shaping the atmosphere, cultural encounters, and memories that stay with visitors long after the final competition. “Stars Align” places Los Angeles’s identity as a city of imagination and possibility at the center of that story. With its blend of sporting history, entertainment, distinctive neighborhoods, and Southern California landscapes, the 2028 Games offer an opportunity to experience the city through a global celebration that extends well beyond the stadium.

item.title: Hollywood Storytelling Takes Center Stage at the LA28 Olympic Games
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games in Los Angeles are bringing together two defining expressions of the city’s global identity: sport and entertainment. LA28 has appointed acclaimed film producer Kathleen Kennedy as Head of Ceremonies and Content, where she will lead the development and delivery of all four Opening and Closing Ceremonies. An eight-time Academy Award nominee and former president of Lucasfilm, Kennedy has helped shape some of cinema’s most recognizable films and franchises, with more than 70 feature film credits. She joins Executive Producer Peter Rice, Creative Director Ben Winston, and veteran ceremonies producer Scott Givens as preparations move toward production. The Olympic Opening Ceremony is scheduled for July 14, 2028, with the Paralympic Games following in August. Across iconic Los Angeles venues, including the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, the ceremonies will draw on the city’s creative influence to introduce the Games to a global audience.

The Curated Take

Major sporting events offer a rare opportunity for a destination to tell its story on a truly global stage. For Los Angeles, that story naturally extends beyond the competition itself, drawing on a cultural identity shaped by film, music, entertainment, and an enduring ability to create spectacle. Kennedy’s appointment brings considerable storytelling experience to that ambition. The ceremonies will be an important part of how visitors and billions of viewers encounter Los Angeles in 2028, positioning the city not simply as a host, but as part of the experience.

item.title: Kanana Nyana: An Intimate Wilderness Retreat in the Okavango Delta
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The newest addition to Ker & Downey Botswana, Kanana Nyana has welcomed its first guests to the forested islands of Botswana’s Okavango Delta, offering an intimate safari experience shaped by the landscape rather than imposed upon it. With just four suites overlooking the floodplain and Xudum Channel, the camp takes its name from the Setswana word nyana, meaning small. Its architecture follows the natural contours of the setting, with elevated decks designed to protect tree roots and preserve the movement of water and wildlife. Interiors draw inspiration from the surrounding trees, waterways, and seasonal colors, incorporating botanical artwork, locally crafted joinery, and natural materials. The result is a secluded wilderness retreat where thoughtful design, regional craftsmanship, and a close connection to nature define the experience.

The Curated Take

In a landscape as extraordinary as the Okavango Delta, the most meaningful luxury may be knowing when not to compete with the surroundings. Kanana Nyana’s small scale allows the wilderness to remain the central presence, while its design reveals a remarkable attention to the details of place, from the changing colors of nearby trees to the waterways that shape the islands. There is something quietly compelling about a safari camp that seeks not to stand apart from its environment, but to help guests notice it more deeply. Here, intimacy is not simply a matter of fewer suites. It is a way of experiencing the Delta.

item.title: Beyond the Signal: Four Remote Escapes for a Deeper Connection with Nature
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For travelers willing to venture beyond familiar routes and the reach of reliable connectivity, Untamed Travelling curates journeys into some of the world’s more remote wilderness landscapes. In northern India, Vanghat is a secluded eco-lodge on the Western Ramganga River, deep within the Corbett Tiger Reserve, reached by a cross-country hike or a combination of four-wheel drive and river raft. Farther north, a snow leopard expedition into Ladakh takes travelers into the Himalayas, with stays at Rumbak Wildlife Lodge on the edge of Hemis National Park. In East Africa, Alex Walker’s Serian offers intimate safari camps in the wilderness areas of Kenya and Tanzania, while South Africa’s Xaus Lodge places guests in the Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park, where individual chalets look directly onto the surrounding landscape. With limited or no connectivity at several of these properties, each experience offers a rare opportunity to step away from digital distractions and give the natural world undivided attention.

The Curated Take

There is a particular kind of extraordinary that only emerges when the familiar conveniences of travel fall away. A lodge reached by river, a mountain expedition in search of an elusive animal, or a night in the Kalahari beyond the reach of a phone signal asks something different of the traveler: patience, curiosity, and a willingness to be fully present. These destinations are not simply remote for the sake of distance. Their appeal lies in the access they offer to landscapes and wildlife that remain largely beyond the everyday frame of experience. In an increasingly connected world, the freedom to be unreachable may be one of travel’s most meaningful luxuries.

item.title: Saba: The Caribbean’s Quietest Kind of Escape
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Just five square miles in size, with a population of approximately 2,000, Saba offers a distinctly different perspective on Caribbean travel. Known as the “Unspoiled Queen of the Caribbean,” the small Dutch Caribbean island has resisted large-scale development, with just five hotels and approximately 140 guest rooms preserving a sense of intimacy rarely found elsewhere in the region. Its dramatic volcanic landscape encompasses 20 hiking trails, five distinct microclimates, and Mount Scenery, the highest point in the Kingdom of the Netherlands at 887 meters. Trails wind through lush rainforest, cloud-covered mountainsides, and changing landscapes, while the surrounding waters are protected as a marine park. In Windwardside, a charming village retains a strong local character, offering another way to experience an island whose appeal rests as much in its atmosphere as its natural beauty.

The Curated Take

Saba’s distinction is not simply that it is small, but that it has preserved the qualities that make a place feel like itself. There are no sprawling resort developments competing for attention, only a remarkable landscape, a close-knit community, and the freedom to experience the Caribbean at a different pace. For travelers accustomed to destinations defined by their amenities and activity, Saba offers another kind of discovery: the pleasure of finding a place where nature sets the rhythm and the absence of crowds becomes a luxury in its own right.

item.title: The Luxury of Stillness in North Carolina’s Blue Ridge Mountains
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In the Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina, Art of Living Retreat Center offers a different expression of luxury, one shaped by space, stillness, and a deeper connection to the natural world. Set amid mountain scenery and seasonal foliage, the retreat brings together immersive wellness programs in meditation, breathwork, silence, and Ayurvedic practices. Guests can step away from the pace of everyday life and enter experiences designed to encourage reflection, mindful movement, and a renewed awareness of the present. As interest in restorative travel grows, the center speaks to travelers seeking more than an escape: an opportunity to find perspective in the quiet rhythms of nature and in the simple act of being still.

The Curated Take

Not every extraordinary journey is measured by how far it takes a traveler or how much it allows them to see. Sometimes, its value lies in what falls away: the noise, the demands, and the constant pull of connectivity. Art of Living Retreat Center offers a compelling perspective on wellness travel, where the mountain landscape becomes part of the experience and stillness is not an absence of activity, but an invitation to pay closer attention. It is a reminder that restoration can be its own form of discovery.

item.title: Orient Express Corinthian Brings a New Era of Sailing Luxury to the Caribbean
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Following a transatlantic crossing from Lisbon via the Azores, Orient Express Corinthian has arrived in Bridgetown, Barbados, beginning a Caribbean season that will extend through the Bahamas and Florida before returning to Europe in spring 2027. The 220-meter sailing yacht will connect destinations including the British Virgin Islands, Anguilla, Saint Martin, Saint-Barthélemy, Antigua, Barbuda, Barbados and Puerto Rico through voyages designed to make the passage itself part of the experience. Its January itinerary from Saint Martin to San Juan, Puerto Rico, includes stops in St. Kitts and Nevis, Antigua, Anguilla and Virgin Gorda, home to the celebrated Baths. Designed by architect Maxime d’Angeac, the yacht features 54 suites with panoramic sea views and dedicated butler service, five restaurants overseen by 18-Michelin-starred chef Yannick Alléno, a Guerlain Spa, eight bars and a marina. Three SolidSail rigs, supported by hybrid LNG propulsion, bring an innovative approach to wind-powered luxury travel.

The Curated Take

There is a distinction between traveling through the Caribbean and experiencing it from the sea. A sailing journey offers a changing perspective on the region, connecting islands and coastlines through the passages between them rather than treating each destination as an isolated stop. With its combination of expansive suites, fine dining and advanced sailing technology, Orient Express Corinthian brings the romance of ocean travel into a contemporary luxury setting. Its arrival also signals a new chapter for the Caribbean’s luxury cruise landscape, where the vessel itself becomes as significant as the destinations along the way.
